newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle poised to sell $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle poised to sell $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $66.00 per cwt early Wednesday were passed by owners asking mostly $68.00, but early indications point to sales later at $67.00, feedlot sources said.
"Judging by all the posturing going on right now, it looks like we're going to trade at $67.00," one Kansas feedlot manager said.

Lower beef prices this week dulled outlooks for $68.00 and offset potential support from ideas packers were short of live inventories, sources said. Sales last week were at $67.00 in moderate to heavy volume.
Owners also were expected to accept $67.00 bids so they could remain current with marketings, especially as milder weather improves rates of weight gains, sources noted.
The pulling ahead of cattle last fall and winter, along with severe weather from mid-December through mid-January in some areas had kept weights as much as 20 lbs below a year ago.

Average weights last week were about four lbs under a year ago, USDA statistics showed. At $67.00, cattle owners' profits ranged $20.00 to $35.00 per head, depending on feed costs and other price factors, several feedlot sources concurred.
